description: I am a Software Engineering graduate interested in AI, machine learning, software development, and space technology. I plan to build an innovative solution using NASA's open data for the Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary:
ExoSphere is an interactive web platform that makes NASA's SPHEREx infrared sky observations accessible to everyone. Developed for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, it allows users to search real SPHEREx observations by sky coordinates, visualize FITS-derived astronomical images, compare observations over time, and explore spectral information across 102 infrared channels.

The platform combines astronomical data access with interactive visualization to simplify the exploration of complex scientific archives. Its temporal comparison and blink functionality help users visually investigate differences between observations, while the spectral explorer offers another way to examine infrared data.

Our goal is to make real astronomical observations easier to explore and help bridge the gap between scientific archives and public engagement with space science.
details:
Overview

ExoSphere is an interactive web application that makes real NASA SPHEREx observations accessible through a visual exploration experience.

Features

  • Sky Explorer: Search sky regions using Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec), retrieve genuine SPHEREx observations, and view FITS-derived astronomical image previews.
  • Temporal Comparison: Select observations and compare their images using an interactive blink feature to visually investigate differences over time.
  • Spectral Explorer: Explore spectral information from SPHEREx data across 102 nominal spectral channels.
  • Discover: An accessible interface for exploring astronomical observations.

Technology Stack

Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, HTTPX, Astropy, and NumPy.

Data: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) SPHEREx observations.

Impact and Creativity

ExoSphere simplifies access to complex astronomical data by bringing observation search, image visualization, temporal comparison, and spectral exploration into one interactive platform. It helps students, astronomy enthusiasts, and curious members of the public engage with real infrared observations.

The application is an exploration and visualization tool. It does not claim to automatically detect planets or discover moving objects.
